title: Exact localization and identity unit law for varying-ring open extension
statement:
Let $R_n$ be arbitrary commutative rings with maps $\varphi_n:R_{n+1}\to R_n$. Use the ordinary module-system categories and operations [def-sp-varying-ring-operations]. For a scheme $X$, let $L=L_{1_X}$ be ordinary inverse image, $B=(1_X)_{!,\bullet}$ ordinary open extension, and $e_X:L\simeq\mathrm{id}$ the inverse-image identity. Define $b_X:B\simeq\mathrm{id}$ as its unit-preserving left-adjoint comparison under $B\dashv L$. Let $J_{1_X}=D(B)$, and let $j_X:J_{1_X}\simeq\mathrm{id}$ be the specified derived identity comparison adjoint to $g_X:D(L)\simeq\mathrm{id}$ under the chosen derived open adjunction. Then $j_X$ equals the localization $D(b_X)$ followed by the exact-derived identity comparison. Moreover, for the specified open compositor $j_{1_X,1_X}:J_{1_X}J_{1_X}\simeq J_{1_X1_X}$,
$$ \operatorname{transport}_{1_X1_X=1_X}\circ j_{1_X,1_X}=J_{1_X}(j_X).$$
These are equalities of derived natural transformations on all unbounded complexes of systems.

proof.text: Write $\mathscr S=\mathscr S_X$, $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to LB$ for the ordinary open unit, and $\eta^D:\mathrm{id}\to GJ$ for the specified derived open unit, where $G=D(L)$ and $J=D(B)$. The operations of [def-sp-varying-ring-operations] are additive and exact here. Their specified exact derived adjunction is the localization of the ordinary one, as in [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction]; thus $\eta^D$ is the localization of $\eta$ with the exact-composition and identity comparisons inserted. The inverse-image identity $g=g_X$ is likewise the localization of $e=e_X$ followed by the exact-derived identity comparison (the defining inverse-image normalization). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] with $(L_1,R_1)=(B,L)$, $(L_2,R_2)=(\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id})$, and $\delta=e^{-1}$. The specified $b=b_X$ is characterized by $L(b_M)\circ\eta_M=e_M^{-1}$ for every $M\in\mathscr S$.

proof.text: Let $h:J\to\mathrm{id}$ be $D(b)$ followed by the exact-derived identity comparison. Apply [lem-sp-exact-derived-transformation-pasting] to the last unit equation. With the normalizations of step 1 it gives $G(h_K)\circ\eta^D_K=g_K^{-1}$ for every derived object $K$. The same equation characterizes the specified $j_X$ by [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation], now with $(L_1,R_1)=(J,G)$, $(L_2,R_2)=(\mathrm{id},\mathrm{id})$ and $\delta=g^{-1}$. Uniqueness therefore gives $j_X=h$, proving the first assertion as an equality of natural transformations.

proof.text:
After transport along $1_X1_X=1_X$, write $c:L\to LL$ for the ordinary inverse-image compositor and $k:BB\to B$ for the specified ordinary open compositor. These are the adjoint comparisons of [def-sp-varying-ring-operations]. By [lem-sp-varying-ring-pullback-unit-coherence] at $f=1_X$, $e_{LM}\circ c_M=\mathrm{id}_{LM}$, so $c_M=e_{LM}^{-1}$. The composite adjunction $BB\dashv LL$ has unit $L(\eta_{BM})\circ\eta_M$ by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] to this adjunction and $B\dashv L$, with $\delta=c$, characterizes $k$ uniquely by
$$LL(k_M)\circ L(\eta_{BM})\circ\eta_M=c_{BM}\circ\eta_M.$$

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), ordinary open adjunction; the identity-coherence calculations are written by the worker, with the exact localization convention of def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction.

proof.text:
The natural transformation $B(b):BB\to B$ satisfies this equation. Indeed naturality of $\eta$ at $b_M$, the equation of step 1, and naturality of $e$ at $\eta_M$, respectively, give
$$\begin{aligned}
LL(B(b_M))\circ L(\eta_{BM})\circ\eta_M
&=L(\eta_M)\circ L(b_M)\circ\eta_M\\
&=L(\eta_M)\circ e_M^{-1}\\
&=e_{LBM}^{-1}\circ\eta_M
=c_{BM}\circ\eta_M.
\end{aligned}$$
Here the first equality is $L$ applied to $LB(b_M)\circ\eta_{BM}=\eta_M\circ b_M$, followed by $\eta_M$; the third rearranges $e_{LBM}\circ L(\eta_M)=\eta_M\circ e_M$. The uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] now yields $k_M=B(b_M)$ for every $M$, hence $k=B(b)$ as natural transformations.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), ordinary open adjunction; the identity-coherence calculations are written by the worker, with the exact localization convention of def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction.

proof.text:
First localize the characterizing equation for $k$ from step 3 using [lem-sp-exact-derived-transformation-pasting]. The localized units are precisely the chosen derived units by [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction], and the inverse-image compositor is its specified exact localization. By [def-sp-varying-ring-operations] the specified open compositor is the unit-preserving adjoint comparison. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation], applied to the composite derived open adjunction and the derived open adjunction for $1_X1_X$, identifies the localization of the ordinary open compositor, with exact-composition comparisons inserted, with $j_{1_X,1_X}$. Now localize $k=B(b)$ by the same pasting statement. Localization preserves whiskering with the precise exact-composition and identity comparisons, so this gives
$$\operatorname{transport}_{1_X1_X=1_X}\circ j_{1_X,1_X}=J(h).$$
Substitute $h=j_X$ from step 2. All cited localizations and unit equations are on the entire unbounded derived category; no boundedness, flatness or coefficient-evaluation assumption has entered.

Step 4: I recomputed the three naturality equalities (eta at b_M, the step-1 equation, e at eta_M) and get k=B(b), the outer whiskering, consistent with J_{1_X}(j_X); the elementary flag is justified. Step 5: localizing the k-equation and k=B(b) via the pasting lemma gives transport∘j_{1,1}=J(j_X), consistent with the Lean jComp being the localized moduleJComp.
